newsitem.title: FRANCE: France, New Zealand take further step to heal ties.
newsitem.headline: France, New Zealand take further step to heal ties.

text.p: France and New Zealand took a further step towards burying a row over French nuclear weapons testing on Tuesday, saying it was time to open a new era in their relationship.

New Zealand Foreign Minister Don McKinnon, the most senior government member to visit Paris since French nuclear testing in 1995 and 1996 outraged Wellington, met for talks with his counterpart, Herve de Charette.
The ministers told reporters they agreed over lunch to use their common interests in the South Pacific to initiate closer political, economic and cultural ties.
They said they would develop common aid initiatives to South Pacific island nations, increase joint maritime surveillance efforts and boost shared disaster relief.
"I can sum it all up by saying this is April in Paris and there's a new spring in the relationship," McKinnon said.
De Charette said New Zealand Prime Minister Jim Bolger would visit Paris soon and he himself would travel to Wellington before the end of the year.
"What we want is to reinforce our political relations, our diplomatic dialogue and the development of our economic relations," de Charette said.

New Zealand spearheaded an international campaign against French nuclear tests, sending a navy ship to shepherd protest yachts and trying unsuccessfully at the International Court of Justice to win an injunction stopping the blasts.
The row plunged relations to their lowest point since 1985, when French secret agents blew up the Greenpeace protest ship Rainbow Warrior in Auckland harbour, killing one man.
But McKinnon said all that was in the past.
"This has been the most comprehensive, the most productive and the most progressive dialogue I've had with the French foreign minister ever in my seven years," he said.
